text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own. In many ministries, senior grades skew male, so a four-man panel can arise by chance from the available pool. It matters as context, not as proof — and leading with it can make a strong case look weak.

Your stronger ground is procedural: two weeks' silence on a written explanation. In most jurisdictions public bodies owe unsuccessful shortlisted candidates reasons, often within a set deadline. Chase that formally, in writing, citing the relevant rule, and ask for the scoring criteria, weightings and your scores against the successful candidate's.

If those documents show criteria shifted after shortlisting, or "international projects" was weighted in late, the panel's composition becomes meaningful corroboration. Until then, hold it in reserve.
